default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-478.title: Multi-session closing-extreme touch fade
E-478.hypothesis: The highest/lowest SESSION CLOSE of the last n sessions is where overnight holders last accepted price; a bar that probes that line and closes back away from it meets passive supply/demand, so fade it.

E-479.title: Multi-session last-hour edge touch fade
E-479.hypothesis: The extremes printed in the final hour of recent sessions are where late positions were squeezed in or out; a probe of that edge that closes back is a stale-level rejection, fade it.

E-480.title: Second-extreme robust edge fade
E-480.hypothesis: The single most extreme daily high/low of the last n sessions is often a one-off spike; the SECOND most extreme is the level the market keeps defending. A probe that closes back is fade material.

E-481.title: Price-time correlation trend onset
E-481.hypothesis: When session price correlates almost perfectly with time over a window, the move is orderly (one-sided flow, few pullbacks); the first bar where this trend quality is reached marks a persistent program, follow it.

E-482.title: Supertrend flip follow
E-482.hypothesis: An ATR-based trailing line flips only when price travels against the trend by several ranges, which means stops of the old trend are run and new-direction orders enter; follow the flip.

E-483.title: Multi-session floor-pivot R1/S1 touch fade
E-483.hypothesis: Pivots built from the last n sessions' high, low and close are used by many discretionary traders; R1/S1 act as self-fulfilling turning points, so a touch that closes back is faded.

E-484.title: Double-EMA slope turn follow
E-484.hypothesis: A double exponential average removes most lag; its slope changing sign is an early sign that short-term order flow has turned, before slower averages show it.

E-485.title: Relative Vigor Index signal cross from the wrong side
E-485.hypothesis: RVI measures how far bars close from their open relative to their range; a cross of its smoothed signal while still on the opposite side of zero marks the first bar-shape evidence that conviction has switched.

E-486.title: Adaptive-average (KAMA) cross follow
E-486.hypothesis: Kaufman's adaptive average hugs price when the move is efficient and flattens in noise, so a close through it with the average already sloping that way happens mainly in efficient moves; follow it.

E-487.title: Average-high/low activator break
E-487.hypothesis: A close beyond the mean of the last n highs (or lows) means price left the area where recent supply (demand) was working; the Gann Hi-Lo activator logic says follow it.
